title: Comparative Analysis of Business Process Digital Twins and Simulation Models: A Case Study in Drone Production
abstract: This paper investigates the theoretical and practical foundations and the distinctions between business process digital twins and business process simulation models. The research includes an overview of simulation methodologies and the concept of digital twins, followed by a case study involving drone production. In the case study, both a simulated production model and a digital twin of the drone production are developed and analyzed. The results demonstrate that there is no significant deviation between the simulated model and the digital twin, confirming that the digital twin operates accurately and reflects real-world conditions. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the intersection between digital twin technology and simulations and indicates that simulation models can be used to validate the correct execution and fidelity of digital twins in a modern production environment, as well as provide insight into their interrelationships and respective roles in business process optimization.

title: From Simulation to Synthesis: A Review of Modified Drone Simulators as Digital Twin and Prototyping Platforms
abstract: The escalating complexity of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems is driving a shift toward simulationdriven design. This review analyzes the transformation of traditional drone simulators into foundational digital twin (DT) and advanced prototyping platforms. Synthesizing research from 2018 to 2025, we present a comprehensive taxonomy of simulator modifications, including high-fidelity physics, DT integration, modular prototyping, and AI validation environments. A critical trend identified is the use of bidirectional data links for real-time synchronization between physical assets and their virtual counterparts. While significant progress exists, challenges remain in seamless sim-to-real transfer and standardized benchmarking. Ultimately, these augmented simulators promise to revolutionize the UAV lifecycle, paving the way for autonomous digital twins and cloud-based collaborative design.

title: UAV Radio Communication Modeling for Digital Twin Inclusion
abstract: In this work we present a flexible methodology for the modeling of UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) radio communications for its inclusion as a radio link module on a Digital Twin (DT). The main purpose of implementing and integrating this module is to characterize and assess the communication link and to foresee conflicting issues due to distance, the environment, the positions and orientation of the aircraft relative to the pilot, and other phenomena. The module is based on an experimentally obtained Path Loss (PL) model during flights and drone-antenna radiation patterns obtained by means of full wave electromagnetic simulations performed with CST Microwave Studio software. This approach allows modeling the Radio Frequency (RF) link between a UAV and its controller. The presented work focuses on implementing a specific drone (an hexacopter), antenna and payloads (No payload, LiDAR and a Jetson), but it is important to note that the developed methodology is easily adaptable to different aerial platforms (drones and their structural materials and payloads), environments (e.g. sub-urban, agronomic), antenna type and its position on the UAV, radio propagation models, etc. Finally, the simulated flight results showed agreement between the estimations and the PL measured during the experimental flights, validating the presented methodology to be implemented for a Digital Twin setup.

title: Efficient Aerodynamic Surrogate Modeling of Switchblade UAVs for Digital Twin
abstract: Aerodynamic modeling of aircraft is a complex and computationally intensive task. To accelerate the optimization process of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), surrogate models have been proposed. This paper presents an active learning algorithm based on a correlation factor. This algorithm combines the Euclidean distance of the nearest neighbors and the bias of variance estimation to achieve higher accuracy with fewer aerodynamic data points. The performance of the obtained results is evaluated using two two-dimensional test functions, demonstrating that the proposed active learning method outperforms the classical random sampling technique. Finally, this algorithm is used to establish the digital aerodynamic twin model of the Switchblade UAV.

title: Enhancing Data-driven Modelling of UAV Digital Twin System with Generated Time-Series Data
abstract: Data-driven modeling is a core enabling technology of UAV digital twin systems, playing a crucial role in flight state prediction, trajectory optimization, and real-time monitoring tasks. By simulating UAV flight trajectories, states, and key control parameters in the digital twin system, the digital twin provides auxiliary decision-making support, optimizes scheduling, and reduces wear and tear on physical equipment. However, in the early stages of system deployment, insufficient accumulation of historical data, along with sparse and incomplete sensor data, limits the integrity of system modeling and the accuracy of physical-world predictions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a diffusion model-based time-series data synthesis method to generate additional samples that align with real data distributions, enhancing the early-stage modeling capability of UAV digital twin systems. This approach enables model training under data-scarce conditions, improving the stability and generalization of flight predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method offers significant advantages in real-time prediction and optimized scheduling of UAV digital twin systems, not only accelerating the construction of the digital twin system but also effectively enhancing prediction accuracy and overall system reliability.

title: The Digital Twin Channel Model Based on Markov Chain for UAV Networks
abstract: Aiming at the highly dynamic channels of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks, this paper proposes a digital twin channel model (DTCM) based on Markov chain as the fast channel simulator to characterize dynamic channel behavior. The proposed model extracts key deployment information of user and base station, as well as large-scale and small-scale channel fading parameters, through data interaction between users and UAV base station. In addition, we adopt a three-state Markov channel configuration corresponding to good, normal, and poor channel qualities. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed model accurately characterizes the channel status under different deployments scenarios. It is shown that this work provides a practical tool for effective channel simulation in UAV networks.

title: Physics-Aware Multichannel Vector Quantization for Hybrid Digital Twin Modeling of UAV Systems
abstract: As Big Data technologies continue to transform industrial manufacturing, digital twin (DT) systems powered by artificial intelligence are becoming key enablers in shaping the emerging low-altitude economy. Among these, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems play a central role. However, building reliable DTs for UAVs remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of sensor data, complex spatiotemporal distributions, and nonlinear interactions within system dynamics. In this work, we propose a fusion framework for UAV-oriented DT modeling that integrates physical priors with data-driven learning, tailored for enhanced DT modeling of UAVs. The method is centered on a multichannel soft vector quantization mechanism, which performs feature clustering across heterogeneous sensor modalities and time scales, enabling robust fusion of multisource data. By embedding physics-aware constraints and leveraging a hybrid fusion strategy, the model enhances generalization under real-world uncertainties. We validate our method by developing a complete UAV DT framework and collecting a large-scale dataset that integrates both simulated and real flight data. Extensive evaluations across hovering, takeoff, tour, and forward flight missions demonstrate superior fidelity and robustness compared to conventional DT models. This work contributes a scalable UAV DT architecture with strong fusion capability and provides open-source tools for advancing self-evolving DT systems in dynamic environments.

title: Evolutionary Optimization of Underwater Drone Swarm Formation for Reliable Communication
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication presents severe limitations in bandwidth, latency, and noise, affecting the coordination of autonomous drone swarms. An evolutionary optimization algorithm for swarm formation is proposed, based on a cooperative game model. Each agent adapts its position to maximize a shared payoff function combining link quality, connectivity, and coverage. The optimization is performed through a GA and validated by a digital twin simulating acoustic propagation, interference, and environmental noise. Results show higher mean SNR and improved network connectivity compared to fixed and random formations. Encryption and spreadspectrum modulation ensure secure operation.

title: Open RAN Internet of Drones: Digital Twin-Driven Multi-Agent RL for Interference Management
abstract: Open radio access network (O-RAN), which enables centralized coordination and intelligent resource control, is a promising architecture for multi-cell Internet of Drones (IoD) networks. However, strong inter-cell inter-drone interference–driven by line-of-sight air-to-ground links–and stringent latency under finite-blocklength (FBL)-coded transmission severely limit uplink data acquisition in IoD networks. This letter addresses these challenges through a radio resource optimization framework that maximizes uplink sum rate while meeting minimum-rate requirements under FBL constraint. The NP-hardness and global channel state information requirements make the optimization problem intractable for practical deployments. To overcome these challenges, we propose a two-stage optimization that includes proportional-fair resource-block scheduling followed by multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-enabled uplink power control. We also develop a double deep Q-network with prioritized experience replay and action masking to improve convergence, stability, and constraint satisfaction. To enable safe and scalable DRL training, a 3D geo-referenced digital twin built on NVIDIA Sionna is used for offline policy learning under site-specific radio frequency (RF) propagation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves faster convergence and higher uplink sum rate than baselines under FBL regimes.

title: A Hybrid Simulation Modeling Within a Digital Twin Framework of AGV-Drone Systems
abstract: Integrating Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGVs) and multi-copter drones, or AGV-drone systems, can potentially enhance efficiency and manipulation in intralogistics operations. While AGVs provide reliable, safe, and energy-efficient ground-based movement, drones offer rapid aerial mobility, making their collaboration promising. However, implementing this system is challenging as it involves collaborating with indoor drones. In particular, the testing phase can be unsafe and expensive because of the high probability of crashes due to the lack of technological advancement in this domain. Primarily, the communication protocols become complicated once the system scales. A digital twin (DT) methodology can help mitigate these risks and improve scalability. This study presents the simulation aspects of a work-in-progress DT for the AGV-drone system. Here, as a work-in-progress DT, the hardware-in-the-loop feature intends to help communicate within the system and build a DT testing environment.

title: Flight State Calibration of Digital Twin Models for UAV Swarms
abstract: Digital twin network (DTN) technology provides significant support for intelligent applications of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms. However, related research focuses on DTN applications and lacks attention to the construction and maintenance of high-fidelity digital twin (DT) models. In this paper, we first develop a DT simulation platform for UAV swarms. Then, a dynamic data-driven DT model calibration scheme is proposed on the example of the most fundamental flight state of a UAV. The scheme utilizes parameter identification to estimate offline the key parameters of the measurement model and system deviations. Furthermore, the flight state is corrected online utilizing data assimilation actuated on the actual and virtual data. Simulation experiments on the DT simulation platform are conducted, and the effects of data sampling rate on calibration accuracy and computational load are analyzed. The results demonstrate that parameter identification and data assimilation significantly improve the fidelity of the DT model in terms of the optimal sub-pattern assignment (OSPA) metric to different degrees.

title: Centralized and Reliable Digital Twin Models for Smart City's Buildings Protection during Disaster
abstract: Digital Twin is one of the fast-growing technology digitalization space which needs to complete Smart City's problem areas. Digital twin is virtual representation of physical things or assets or process in a connected network. The data from Physical asset or things IOT Devices, Sensors, Cameras needs to be collected in a large cloud store which contains the engineering data like machine diagrams or flow charts, building blueprint, building electrical map or waterline map, Building information Model, 3D images, Computer Aided Design (CAD), controls data IOT Sensors, IOT Gateway, Drones, Cameras, etc. and supporting data. This research paper narrates the different types of digital twin with a use case of Smart Building and how it should be protected during disaster time with different technologies and dataset

title: On Constructing Efficient UAV Aerodynamic Surrogate Models for Digital Twins
abstract: Aerodynamic modeling and optimization for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are complex and computationally intensive tasks. Surrogate models have emerged as a powerful tool for increasing efficiency in the aircraft design and optimization process. We review and evaluate some modeling techniques, such as artificial neural networks and support vector regression, showing that Gaussian process regression generally provides a well-performing solution to this type of problem. We propose an active learning algorithm based on the relevance factor, that combines bias estimated from nearest-neighbor Euclidean distance and variance, to achieve higher accuracy with fewer compuational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. The obtained performance is evaluated using four 2-D test functions and an experimental CFD case, indicating that the proposed active learning approach outperforms classical random sampling techniques. Thanks to this architecture, the development process of a new commercial UAV can be significantly streamlined by expediting the testing phase through the use of DTs modeled more efficiently.

title: Behaviour Modelling of Self-Learning UAVs using Agent-Based Simulation for Understanding Battery Depletion Rates and Operational Lifespan
abstract: Autonomous self-learning Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) embody the future of swarm intelligence and energy-conscious mission planning. Previous research work in UAV optimization is mostly dependent on control-theoretic or reinforcementlearning approaches with minimum real-time adaptability to evolving behavior. This paper introduces an Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) approach in $\mathbf{R}$ that models emergent learning, energy usage, and endurance behavior of self-learning UAVs. The virtual data were created with ten control parameters and were utilized to simulate $\mathbf{1 0 0}$ UAV agents across 200 mission steps. Three self-organizing UAV types emerged from the unsupervised k -means clustering of the identified behavioral archetypes. Statistical analysis by linear mixed-effects model and KaplanMeier survival analysis demonstrated substantial variance in battery depletion rates and operation lifetime between behavior clusters. The “BalancedStrategist” UAVs showed better energy efficiency and mission endurance, whereas high-aggression agents showed fast battery degradation and reduced survival time. The proposed model effectively combined behavioral, physical, and energy dynamics within a single simulated environment. Results provide a measurable connection between learning rate, endurance and aggression in autonomous UAVs and provide predictive understanding for optimizing swarm coordination and battery-conscious control approaches in industrial, defense, and environmental monitoring scenarios.

title: Deep Learning Driven Security in Digital Twins of Drone Network
abstract: This study aims to explore the security issues and computational intelligence of drone information system based on deep learning. Targeting at the security issues of the drone system when it is attacked, this study adopts the improved long short-term memory (LSTM) network to analyze the cyber physical system (CPS) data for prediction from the perspective of predicting the control signal data of the system before the attack occurs. At the same time, the differential privacy frequent subgraph (DPFS) is introduced to keep data privacy confidential, and the digital twins technology is used to map the operating environment of the drone in the physical space, and an attack prediction model for drone digital twins CPS is constructed based on differential privacy-improved LSTM. Finally, the tennessee eastman (TE) process is undertaken as a simulation platform to simulate the constructed model so as to verify its performance. In addition, the proposed model is compared with the Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) and Attention-BiLSTM models proposed by other scholars. It was found that the root mean square error (RMSE) of the proposed model is the smallest (0.20) when the number of hidden layer nodes is 26. Comparison with the actual flow value shows that the proposed algorithm is more accurate with better fitting. Therefore, the constructed drone attack prediction model can achieve higher prediction accuracy and obvious better robustness under the premise of ensuring errors, which can provide experimental basis for the later security and intelligent development of drone system.

title: A Survey on LLM-Enabled UAV Digital Twins for Internet of Vehicles Systems
abstract: Vehicular Digital Twins (VDTs) are emerging as a core enabler for real-time monitoring, simulation, and intelligent control in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems. While prior research has largely focused on ground vehicles, the integration of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) into vehicular digital twin ecosystems remains underexplored. This paper presents a comprehensive survey on the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in enabling UAV Digital Twins for autonomous and cooperative operations within IoV environments. By conceptualizing UAVs as cyber-physical entities continuously synchronized with their virtual counterparts, we analyze how LLMs act as cognitive engines for high-level reasoning, multimodal perception grounding, natural-language interaction, and adaptive mission planning. The survey introduces an LLM-enabled UAV Digital Twin architecture incorporating edge-cloud collaboration, real-time state mirroring, and safety-aware control. Communication workflows leveraging vehicular networking paradigms such as V2X are discussed to support low-latency synchronization and fleet-level coordination. Key application domains, including disaster response, infrastructure monitoring, and Drone-as-a-Service within IoV systems, are examined. Finally, open challenges related to real-time synchronization, computational constraints, and scalability are highlighted, along with future research directions involving TinyLLMs, federated learning, and edge-enabled digital twin platforms.

title: A Multi-UAV-Enabled CCICI Joint Optimization Framework for Digital Twin Channel Modeling
abstract: To meet the requirements of real-time link sensing and efficient response in channel modeling for sixth-generation (6 G) digital twin (DT) networks, network architectures are evolving toward the convergence of heterogeneous capabilities. In response to this trend, this paper proposes a multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled Communication-Computing-IntelligenceControlling Integrated (CCICI) joint optimization framework to efficiently support the collection and uploading of linkstate information. The proposed framework adopts a hierarchical multi-UAV system, consisting of mobile edge servers with trajectory control and task scheduling capabilities, as well as statically deployed working UAVs, collaboratively performing urban environment data collection, processing, and uploading of link-state information. Under constraints such as UAV maximum flight speed and limited communication resources, the framework jointly optimizes UAV flight trajectories and service scheduling strategies, including movement direction selection and service assignment. A heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (GNN) is utilized to model the complex task dependencies and dynamic communication topology among UAVs. Moreover, a QMIXbased multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) method under the centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm is employed to overcome the limitations of traditional methods in handling dynamic scenarios and partial observability. To guarantee data timeliness and prompt system responsiveness required by DT channel modeling, Age of Information (AoI) and service delay are adopted as the core optimization metrics. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively reduces these two metrics, confirming its effectiveness and stability in dynamic urban environments.

title: Modeling and Control of a Prescribed Fire with UAVs as Sensors and Actuators
abstract: Prescribed fires are critical tools for maintaining ecosystem health, reducing wildfire risk, and promoting biodiversity. However, executing prescribed burns safely and effectively remains challenging due to the inherent complexities of fire behavior and the need for precise real-time control. This work presents a comprehensive framework for modeling and controlling prescribed fires using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as integrated sensing and actuation platforms. A hybrid digital twin approach is proposed, combining physics-based fire propagation model with simulated UAV-based multispectral and thermal imaging sensors. The digital twin enables accurate, dynamic predictions of fire spread, facilitating UAV-based adaptive control strategies. By leveraging UAVs’ ability to autonomously respond to evolving fire conditions, the framework improves the precision, responsiveness, and safety of prescribed fire management compared to traditional methods. This research lays the foundation for autonomous and intelligent wildfire management systems, significantly advancing future land management practices and wildfire mitigation efforts.

title: Digital Twin Modeling of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: The Importance of UAV Simulation in Engineering Practice and Research has Become Increasingly Evident. High Simulation Accuracy, Strong Adaptability, and Environmental Diversity are Primary Requirements. In this paper, leveraging digital twin technology, a precise digital model of physical objects is created, enabling the faithful computer-based recreation of UAV flights in real-world scenarios. The ultimate test results demonstrate that this system meets the requirements for UAV simulation.

title: Bridging Simulation and Reality: A 3D Clustering-Based Deep Learning Model for UAV-Based RF Source Localization
abstract: Localization of radio frequency (RF) sources has critical applications, including search and rescue, jammer detection, and monitoring of hostile activities. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer significant advantages for RF source localization (RFSL) over terrestrial methods, leveraging autonomous 3D navigation and capturing stronger signals at higher altitudes. Recent advancements in deep learning (DL) have further enhanced localization accuracy, particularly for outdoor scenarios. DL models often face challenges in real-world deployment due to training on simulated datasets that do not fully replicate real-world conditions. To address this, we first propose the Enhanced Two-Ray propagation model, reducing the simulation-to-reality gap by improving the accuracy of propagation environment modeling. For RFSL, we propose the 3D Cluster-Based RealAdap-tRNet, a DL-based method that leverages 3D clustering-based feature extraction for robust localization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Enhanced Two-Ray model provides superior accuracy in simulating real-world propagation scenarios. Notably, the 3D Cluster-Based RealAdaptRNet, trained entirely on simulated data, achieves exceptional performance when validated in a real-world setting using the AERPAW physical testbed, with an average localization error of 18.2 m. The proposed approach is computationally efficient—using 33.5× fewer parameters—and generalizes well across diverse trajectories, making it highly suitable for real-world applications.

title: Collection: UAV-Based Wireless Multi-Modal Measurements From AERPAW Autonomous Data Mule (AADM) Challenge in Digital Twin and Real-World Environments
abstract: In this work, we present an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) wireless dataset collected as part of the AERPAW Autonomous Aerial Data Mule (AADM) challenge, organized by the NSF Aerial Experimentation and Research Platform for Advanced Wireless (AERPAW) project. The AADM challenge was the second competition in which an autonomous UAV acted as a data mule, where the UAV downloaded data from multiple base stations (BSs) in a dynamic wireless environment. Participating teams designed flight control and decision-making algorithms for selecting which BSs to communicate with and how to plan flight trajectories to maximize data download within a mission completion time. The competition was conducted in two stages: Stage 1 involved development and experimentation using a digital twin (DT) environment, and in Stage 2, the final test run was conducted on the outdoor testbed. The total score for each team was compiled from both stages. The resulting dataset includes link quality and data download measurements, both in DT and physical environments. Along with the universal software radio peripheral (USRP) measurements used in the contest, the dataset also includes UAV telemetry, Keysight radio frequency sensor position estimates, link quality measurements from long-range (LoRa) receivers, and Fortem radar measurements. It supports reproducible research on autonomous UAV networking, multi-cell association and scheduling, air-to-ground propagation modeling, DT-to-real-world transfer learning, and integrated sensing and communication, which serves as a benchmark for future autonomous wireless experimentation. title: Digital Twin Enabled Simultaneous Learning and Modeling for UAV-Assisted Secure Wireless Sensing in Unknown Environment
abstract: This paper focuses on secure communications in UAV-assisted wireless sensing systems in the presence of a mobile UAV eavesdropper (MUE), without prior information about the traffic demands of ground users (GUs) in the sensing environment. To maximize secrecy performance, we propose a digital-twin enhanced proximal policy optimization (DTEPPO) algorithm that optimizes the GUs' sensing scheduling and the UAVs' trajectory planning and network formation. Unlike traditional reinforcement learning methods that require complete environment-interacted information, we build a digital twin (DT) model using Gaussian process regression (GPR) based on the historical sensing information collected by the UAVs. Moreover, DT model can be dynamically updated by exploiting the PPO algorithm to lean the UAVs' interactions with the environment, continuously enhancing its accuracy and providing a reliable virtual learning environment for fast network adaptation. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed DTEPPO algorithm achieves rapid convergence and improved secure throughput with reduced communication overhead compared to conventional approaches. Moreover, the proposed framework enables simultaneous learning and modeling (SLAM) in an unknown environment, providing a general framework to solve complex network control problems in wireless and mobile systems with high costs of environmental interactions.

title: Integrating drones with digital twins for aerial remote sensing
abstract: Drones are highly autonomous, remote-controlled platforms capable of performing a variety of tasks in diverse environments. A digital twin (DT) is a virtual replica of a physical system. The integration of DT with drones gives the opportunity to manipulate the drone during a mission. In this paper, the architecture of DT is presented in order to explain how the physical environment can be represented. The techniques via which drones are collecting the necessary information for DT are compared as a next step to introduce the main methods that have been applied in DT progress by drones. The findings of this research indicated that the process of incorporating DTs into drones will result in the advancement of readings from all sensors, control code and intelligence. This can be executed on the DTs, remote control for the performance of complex tasks in a variety of application environments, and simulation on the DTs without having an effect on the actual drone. On the other hand, in order to develop three-dimensional representations of structures and construction sites, a method known as photogrammetry is used to generate these models employing drones as aerial scanners. In spite of this, there are a number of technological and social-political obstacles that should be taken in consideration. These challenges include the interoperability of different sensors, the creation of efficiently optimized data processing algorithms, and concerns over data privacy and security.

title: Drones as a Platform for Integrated STEM Education: Bridging Engineering, Programming, and Real-World Applications
abstract: The rapid evolution of unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) is revolutionizing various industrial applications, and their integration into education presents a unique opportunity for comprehensive STEM learning. This paper proposes a curriculum framework that harnesses drones as a versatile platform for integrated STEM education, bridging engineering design, computer programming, and real-world applications. Drawing inspiration from two industrial research projects—one on autonomous drone-based inspection systems for thermal power plant boilers and another on generating synthetic data using digital twins of industrial instruments—we demonstrate how advanced technologies can be adapted for classroom use. Our curriculum is structured into sequential modules that guide students through the process of assembling a modular drone kit, programming autonomous navigation in confined and challenging environments, and implementing computer vision algorithms for defect detection. In doing so, learners engage with fundamental STEM concepts such as aerodynamics, sensor integration, control systems, and machine learning. This hands-on, project-based approach not only cultivates technical proficiency and interdisciplinary problem solving but also fosters critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative skills among students. Furthermore, by simulating real-world industrial challenges, the framework provides educators with a robust model for professional development and curriculum integration. Ultimately, this integrated approach highlights the transformative potential of drone technology to make STEM education more engaging, relevant, and aligned with current industry practices, thereby preparing students to meet future technological challenges.

title: HG-MARL Based Scheduling of Trajectory and Offloading for Layered UAVs-Enabled Digital Twin Channel Modeling in Integrated Communication-Computing-Intelligence-Controlling Network
abstract: As a key paradigm in sixth-generation (6G) systems for enabling physical–virtual mapping and intelligent network management, Digital Twin (DT) networks demand high-precision, low-latency modeling and continuous updates of wireless environments. However, in dynamic urban scenarios, channel conditions are highly non-stationary, and traditional sensing schemes suffer from limitations in coverage, information timeliness, and scheduling efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Integrated Communication-Computing-Intelligence-Controlling (ICCIC) network based on layered uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). The system comprises mobile edge servers (ESs) with trajectory control and scheduling capabilities, and statically deployed working UAVs responsible for wireless channel measurements. The collected data is offloaded to ESs for edge computing and local model construction, which supports subsequent DT channel modeling. A multi-objective optimization problem is formulated to jointly schedule UAV trajectories and data offloading, with Age of Information (AoI) and service delay as performance metrics. The optimization is subject to constraints including maximum task execution time and service fairness. To capture multi-type interactions among UAVs during sensing and coordination, we build a multi-relational heterogeneous graph and encode it with a graph neural network (GNN) to obtain structured system states. On this basis, we adopt a QMIX-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework under centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) to learn cooperative scheduling policies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in sensing timeliness, scheduling responsiveness, and policy convergence, providing robust support for efficient and reliable DT channel modeling.

title: Inverse-Reinforcement Learning for Intention-driven Drone Trajectory Design in Digital Twin Networks
abstract: In this paper, the problem of the trajectory design for an intention-driven drone operating in dynamic wireless network environments is studied. In the considered model, the drone acts as a supplementary base station that navigates among ground user clusters to provide on-demand uplink data access. Given its intended application (e.g traffic monitoring), the drone base station (DBS) prioritizes serving certain clusters (e.g. high-risk highway sections). A digital twin (DT) system, hosted on a central server, creates a virtual representation of the wireless network environment to simulate and predict related changes, at which case the DBS trajectory should also be adjusted. Then, the DT system suggests adjustment of DBS trajectories without guaranteed access to the DBS service priorities, as the DBS may not cooperate with wireless infrastructures for same data collection applications. Such adjustment is posed as an optimization problem whose goal is to find the trajectories with which the fraction of prioritized users served by the DBS is maximized. To solve this problem under unknown DBS intention and unpredictable environment changes, an inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) based DT actuation solution is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate a less than 1% performance gap from the optimal trajectory, without requiring access to confidential service priorities, while exhibiting a 7% improvement compared to the baseline IRL algorithm.

title: Using SysML Models as Digital Twins for Early Validation of Modular Systems and Systems of Systems
abstract: For early validation of system concepts, reviews of SysML models can be complemented by employing simulation models as virtual prototypes. Such simulation models can be gradually expanded into digital twins during system development. However, it is usually difficult to include all relevant physical aspects of the system or its context in such models. Also, the creation of such models is usually laborious. To be able to validate the system concept early without much effort and nevertheless considering the real context and physical details, in this paper the SysML model itself is used as a digital twin to control real prototypes in a real context. To create real prototypes rapidly, already existing components are re-used to set up modular systems or Systems of Systems (SoS). The presented approach has been successfully evaluated through rapid development of an SoS consisting of a drone swarm and an autonomously driving vehicle.

title: Diffusion Models for Smarter UAVs: Decision Making and Modeling
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used in modern communication networks. However, challenges in decision making and digital modeling continue to hinder their rapid development. Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms face limitations such as low sample efficiency and limited data versatility, which are further amplified in UAV communications scenarios. Additionally, digital twin (DT) modeling presents significant challenges in decision making and data management. RL models, often integrated into DT frameworks to address these issues, require large amounts of training data to make accurate predictions. Unlike traditional approaches that focus on class boundaries, diffusion models (DMs)—a new class of generative artificial intelligence (AI)—learn the underlying probability distribution from training data and can generate reliable new patterns based on this learned distribution. DT and RL have complementary roles in enabling intelligent and data-driven UAV operations. DMs further enhance this synergy by addressing data scarcity, improving modeling accuracy, and generating realistic scenarios, which benefit both DT simulations and RL training. In this article, we explore the integration of DMs with RL and DT. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness and benefits of DMs in generating neighbor-velocity estimates in a four-UAV swarm coordination task using deep RL (DRL).

title: Assessing the Effects of Drone Control Interfaces on Situational Awareness and Digital Twin Environment Updates
abstract: Drone swarms are an attractive emerging technology for a wide range of application domains. In particular, mounting cameras on drones allows operators to capture live aerial video feeds to gain situational awareness in regions of interest. Effective visualizations of these video feeds and efficient drone control interfaces are crucial for use cases from emergency zone monitoring over facility surveillance to search and rescue. Recent advances in this field have seen the introduction of 3D digital twin models and real-time visualizations, which impose new possibilities but also challenges for manual and autonomous control interfaces, especially when multiple drones are employed.In this paper, we present a user study (N=23) in which we evaluated and compared different approaches for their usability, artifacts, preference, and resulting situational awareness in a region of interest. Therefore, we used a virtual drone simulation framework in which we modeled five drone control methods: two manually controlled by the user and three autonomously controlled. Our results show a general preference of manual drone control interfaces for tracking single moving targets and autonomous control interfaces for keeping track of regions of interest. Further, regional and coordinated autonomous control interfaces significantly improved situational awareness in regions of interest. We discuss the different trade-offs, implications, and guidelines for choosing effective drone control interfaces in this field.

title: Enhanced Network Metric Prediction for Machine Learning-Based Cyber Security of a Software-Defined UAV Relay Network
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), e.g., drones, have become crucial assets in the military’s fleet of vehicles. UAVs can provide limited bandwidth for tactical communications and can act as relays over battlefields. Modern drones provide much higher bandwidth than their legacy predecessors with dynamic antenna capabilities that would be useful in communicating around obstacles, such as urban corridors formed by rows of tall buildings that limit terrestrial lines of sight and attenuate high frequencies. While it is still more likely that one UAV is used for this purpose, a well-managed cluster of UAVs could increase the functionality of the entire terrestrial-drone network. Software-defined networking (SDN) is recognized as an effective way to manage distributed wireless networks. In our previous research, we used a software-defined UAV (SD-UAV) network to offer organized and secure communication resources and relaying capabilities to soldiers, military vehicles, and assets on the ground in a signal-challenged urban environment. Additionally, we developed a framework for detecting common multiple types of cyberattacks (black hole, gray hole, and jamming) using the Light Gradient Boosting machine learning algorithm. However, zero-day attacks are newly developed cyberattacks that can cause significant harm to the functionality of a SD-UAV network. Due to the novelty of these attacks, there is a lack of data samples for ML model training and testing. In order to tackle this problem, this paper provides a predictive queuing analysis of a SD-UAV network. To our knowledge, no previous work has proposed using queuing analysis to predict network performance statistics of SD-UAV networks for the purpose of enhancing security against zero-day cyberattacks. This analysis allows the network operator to calculate the expected theoretical values of the average interarrival time, transmission delay, and packet count of each SD-UAV in a swarm under normal, non-attack operating conditions. This allows the network operator to establish a normal baseline for ML training in order to compare and detect zero-day attacks by detecting any malicious or abnormal SD-UAV network behavior. In this study, we conduct an analysis, simulation, and discussion of the results of our predictive queuing analysis. Our simulation results confirm the accuracy of our predictive queuing analysis we obtained for the average interarrival times, transmission delay, and packet count for the SD-UAVs in the swarm. Our predictive queuing analysis enables the network operator to predict network performance statistics of the SD-UAVs for the purpose of enhancing security against zero-day cyberattacks.

title: Edge General Intelligence Through World Models, Large Language Models, and Agentic AI: Fundamentals, Solutions, and Challenges
abstract: Edge General Intelligence (EGI) represents a transformative evolution of edge computing, where distributed agents possess the capability to perceive, reason, and act autonomously across diverse, dynamic environments. This vision is increasingly realized through agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems, which often leverage large language models (LLMs) for complex reasoning and planning. However, language-based reasoning alone struggles to capture high-dimensional physical dynamics. Central to overcoming this challenge are world models, which act as proactive internal simulators that not only predict but also actively imagine future trajectories, reason under uncertainty, and plan multi-step actions with foresight. This proactive nature allows agents to anticipate potential outcomes and optimize decisions ahead of real-world interactions. While prior works in robotics and gaming have showcased the potential of world models, their integration into the wireless edge for EGI remains underexplored. This survey bridges this gap by offering a comprehensive analysis of how world models can empower agentic systems at the edge, enhancing their foresight beyond the limits of LLM-based reasoning. We first examine the architectural foundations of world models, including latent representation learning, dynamics modeling, and imagination-based planning. Building on these core capabilities, we illustrate their proactive applications across EGI scenarios such as vehicular networks, uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks, the Internet of Things (IoT) systems, and network functions virtualization, thereby highlighting how they can enhance optimization under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. We then explore their synergy with foundation models and digital twins, positioning world models as the cognitive backbone of EGI. Finally, we highlight open challenges, such as safety guarantees, efficient training, and constrained deployment, and outline future research directions. This survey provides both a conceptual foundation and a practical roadmap for realizing the next generation of intelligent, autonomous edge systems.

title: Heuristic Estimation of Temperature-Dependant Model Parameters of Li-Po Batteries for UAV Applications
abstract: This work deals with the system identification of Thevenin models of Li-Po batteries for UAV applications. Starting from the results of an experimental hybrid pulse-power characterization of a battery pack carried out at different temperatures (0°C, 15°C, 49°C) and within the operative range of state-of-charge (>10%), the model parameters are identified via three heuristic optimization algorithms, based on particle-swarm, teaching-learning and differential evolution techniques. Differently from conventional approaches typically applied by commercial CAE tools (e.g. Matlab), the proposed techniques are directly applied to the whole time history of the measurements. The results highlight that the particle-swarm method exhibits the fastest convergence, but it requires to initially define the algorithm weighing coefficients. This is not needed for teaching-learning based optimization, but computational effort strongly increases to achieve satisfactory accuracy. The differential evolution technique provides intermediate performances, especially if the total computation time is also considered. The case study is referred to the 1850 mAh/6 cells/22.2 V Li-Po battery pack employed in the lightweight fixed-wing UAV Rapier X-25, developed by Sky Eye Systems (Italy).

title: Data-Driven Extraction of Simulation Models for Energy-Oriented Digital Twins of Manufacturing Systems: An Illustrative Case Study
abstract: Manufacturing systems, as significant energy consumers and potential contributors to energy efficiency optimization, play an important role in addressing global energy challenges. Digital Twins utilize available data from smart manufacturing systems to effectively understand and replicate systems' energy-related behaviors. Digital Twins facilitate detailed systems analysis and enable decision support for optimizing energy efficiency through performing relevant ‘what-if” scenario analyses. In this paper, we propose a methodology for data-driven extraction of simulation models for Energy-Oriented Digital Twins of smart manufacturing systems. Through a case study of a data-driven Energy-Oriented Digital Twin for an assembly process of a quadcopter drone part, we illustrate our initial methodology and the related data requirements. Our case study helps comprehend the complexity of extracting Energy-Oriented Digital Twins in smart manufacturing systems, offering insights into the integration of production and energy-related processes and behaviors of the system.

title: AirEye: UAV-Based Intelligent DRL Mobile Target Visitation
abstract: From traffic monitoring to livestock tracking, and military reconnaissance to marine discovery, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are indispensable. Its dependence on a battery for power supply limits the flight time to visit all planned locations. Consequently, target visitation needs to be smart and minimize the mechanical energy. We propose to develop the AirEye UAV-based smart platform that can perform target visitation in the shortest time possible without knowing targets' exact locations, but with a known probabilistic distribution. We show how to integrate a UAV with the proper hardware to control it and execute commands from an on-ground command and control station. A pre-built machine learning model was modified to detect and identify targets, along with a reinforcement learning (RL) model to autonomously navigate the drone and ensure that all targets are visited while consuming minimal energy. We propose a drone energy model that can be used to estimate the total energy consumed by the drone in a complex scenario. We then use this energy model to compare the total energy consumed by the proposed RL-based technique in comparison with two other heuristic strategies, namely, random, and zigzag motion.

title: A Digital-Twin-Empowered Lightweight Model-Sharing Scheme for Multirobot Systems
abstract: Multirobot system for manufacturing is an Industry Internet of Things (IIoT) paradigm with significant operational cost savings and productivity improvement, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are employed to control and implement collaborative productions without human intervention. This mission-critical system relies on 3-dimension (3-D) scene recognition to improve operation accuracy in the production line and autonomous piloting. However, implementing 3-D point cloud learning, such as Pointnet, is challenging due to limited sensing and computing resources equipped with UAVs. Therefore, we propose a digital twin (DT) empowered knowledge distillation (KD) method to generate several lightweight learning models and select the optimal model to deploy on UAVs. With a digital replica of the UAVs preserved at the edge server, the DT system controls the model-sharing network topology and learning model structure to improve recognition accuracy further. Moreover, we employ network calculus to formulate and solve the model sharing configuration problem toward minimal resource consumption, as well as convergence. Simulation experiments are conducted over a popular point cloud data set to evaluate the proposed scheme. Experiment results show that the proposed model-sharing scheme outperforms the individual model in terms of computing resource consumption and recognition accuracy.

title: RDIwS: An Efficient Beamforming-Based Method for UAV Detection and Classification
abstract: The detection and classification of unmanned air vehicles (UAVs) are disturbing challenges within contemporary radar systems, wherein the physical characteristics of UAVs, including their size and radar cross section (RCS), exert a substantial influence on radar’s detection capabilities. Smaller UAVs, characterized by reduced RCS values, often escape radar detection. In response to these challenges, this study introduces an efficient radar signal processing technique based on beamforming, termed range–Doppler integration while steering (RDIwS). RDIwS significantly enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) associated with UAVs, resulting in an increased detection probability and classification accuracy for these UAVs. Importantly, the RDIwS approach demonstrates superior performance to traditional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) methods and established beamforming-based techniques, showcasing its potential to significantly advance UAV detection and classification across various operational contexts. For four targets located at different angles and distances scenario, and at −30 dB SNR and false alarm probability of  $10^{-{5}}$ , the RDIwS beamforming-based method achieved a detection probability of 75% compared to 5% for steering-only beamforming, and no detection for MIMO radar case.

title: A Novel Power Pylon Truss Modeler for LoD3 Reconstruction From ULS Data: Bridging the Gap Between Visualization and Simulation
abstract: Amid growing global electricity demand and increasingly frequent extreme weather events, ensuring the reliable operation of power transmission infrastructure is paramount. A major bottleneck, however, is the generation of high fidelity, truss level [level of detail (LoD3)] pylon models suitable for engineering simulation, because existing methods are largely limited to visual approximation and perform poorly on sparse uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) light detection and ranging [UAV borne laser scanning (ULS)] data. To address this critical gap, we introduce the pylon truss modeler (PTM), a novel algorithm that, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, enables accurate LoD3 reconstruction from challenging ULS data for the first time. PTM has two key innovations: a data enhancement strategy that significantly improves point cloud density and clarity, and a highly efficient “node-first” reconstruction strategy. This framework simplifies reconstruction by reframing it as a “node identification then connection” task and further converts 3-D truss node localization into a 1-D signal processing problem through dimensionality reduction. Experimental validation on an 11 km transmission corridor demonstrates that PTM can reconstruct complex pylon structures with an average point-to-model RMSE ($\text{RMSE}_{p}$) of 0.137 m, a node localization RMSE of 0.098 m, and low normalized graph edit distances of 0.048 and 0.035 for main and diagonal members, respectively. Most importantly, we demonstrate the use of these reconstructed models in finite-element deformation analysis to support preliminary structural-response assessment of in-service pylons. This work not only validates the effectiveness of PTM, but also establishes a novel, noncontact paradigm for transforming real-world sensing data into mechanically analyzable pylon models, thereby bridging the gap between visualization and simulation.

title: Digital Twin Based Design and Flight Feasibility Analysis of an Ornithopter
abstract: Ornithopters are bio-inspired flapping-wing aerial vehicles that offer advantages over conventional unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in terms of low-speed efficiency, maneuverability, and reduced acoustic noise. However, the design of ornithopters is challenging due to the unsteady and nonlinear nature of flapping-wing aerodynamics, making early-stage physical prototyping expensive and time-consuming. This paper presents the design and simulation of a digital twin of an ornithopter for early-stage flight feasibility analysis. A three-dimensional CAD model is developed to extract geometric parameters, followed by mathematical modeling of aerodynamic forces using a quasi-steady lift formulation. The model is implemented in MATLAB to simulate sinusoidal flapping-wing motion under varying flapping frequencies. Simulation results indicate that a minimum flapping frequency of 3.9 Hz is required to satisfy the lift-weight equilibrium condition, validating the effectiveness of the digital twin approach for design verification prior to physical prototyping.

title: Modeling A UAV Surveillance Scenario- An Applied MBSE Approach
abstract: As the complexity of both products and systems increases across a wide range of industry sectors, there has been an influx in demand for methods of system organization and optimization. MBSE enhances the ability to obtain, analyze, communicate, and manage data on a comprehensive architecture of a system. In this study, a military combat surveillance scenario is modeled using SysML generating state machine diagrams and activity diagrams using the Magic Model Analyst execution framework plugin. This study seeks to prove the feasibility of an MBSE-enabled framework using SysML to create and simulate a surveillance system that monitors and reports on the health status and performance of an armored fighting vehicle (combat tank) through an Unmanned Ariel Vehicle (UAV). The Magic System of Systems Architect, which actively promotes system development architectural frameworks, was used to construct SysML-compliant models, allowing the creation of intricate model diagrams. The construction of the UAV surveillance scenario emphasized the capability of modifying a diagram feature and ensuring that the alteration is communicated to all linked model diagrams. This study builds on a previously published MBSE-enabled conceptual framework for creating digital twins. The purpose of this research is to test and validate the framework's procedures.

title: Creating a Digital Twin RL DAA Model to Drone Flight Framework
abstract: This project presents a Digital Twin framework for detect-and-avoid (DAA) research, training, and validation, culminating in real-world flight execution on swarm of UAVs. The system integrates reinforcement learning (RL), simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop execution to evaluate DAA behavior across representative encounter scenarios. The Digital Twin models uncrewed aircraft dynamics, sensor observations, and realistic obstacle geometries—including static infrastructure and moving traffic. These efforts emulate operations involving interactions between cooperative and non-cooperative crewed aircraft with uncrewed aircraft. Each mission produces a CSV log containing the agent’s pose, clearance, time-to-collision (TTC), and event flags; allowing any flight to be reviewed, replayed, and analyzed as needed.The research team developed an end-to-end DAA framework that trains an intelligent avoidance policy in simulation and executes the resulting flight path in a physically identical real-world environment. The system uses Crazyflie 2.0 quadcopters operating within a simulated training environment, which is a digital representation of the University of North Dakota Aerospace indoor swarm testbed at Robin Hall. All simulation, training, and telemetry data are expressed in a shared physical coordinate frame with the origin at the center of the flight area, enabling maneuvering space of ±3.15m longitudinally and ±1.475m laterally and allowing direct correspondence between simulated and real-world execution.Policy training is performed using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), implemented with Stable-Baselines3 on PyTorch. The PPO agent employs an MLP actor-critic architecture. To maximize robustness, three distinct behavioral variants were employed—Red, Blue, and Yellow; each using variant-specific entropy coefficients and learning-rate schedules. These presets allow for the systematic exploration of tradeoffs between exploration, convergence speed, and functionality. Monitoring and management of long-running training is supported through checkpointing, automatic resume, and consistent naming conventions unique to each variant. Training runs automatically save at regular intervals and support training resuming, so a multi-day training campaign never loses progress.Evaluation callbacks log mission-critical metrics including: goal achievement, collision, boundary violation, and timeout rates. These metrics are reported to the user via TensorBoard, enabling continuous monitoring of policy robustness throughout training.Central to the creation of a model capable of both stable and interoperable DAA behavior is the layered curriculum. Training progresses through multiple difficulty levels; the model is exposed to increasing stages of complexity. Agents first master low-risk navigation behaviors before advancing to timed dodge drills and increasingly aggressive challenge layouts. Regulated by these curriculum stages are maneuvering caps, obstacle density, dodge-drill probability, reward bonuses, and penalty scaling. Promotion between training stages is governed by short evaluation windows and explicit performance gates (e.g., goal-rate thresholds), while timeout-based difficulty caps allow improved time-to-goal performance to unlock additional complexity; eventually arriving at the full-complexity scenario. Because each stage has a rigidly refined performance gate, the exact point where a policy struggled can be traced where a policy struggled, allowing targeted correction.The combined RL and Digital Twin framework allows for nuanced analysis, reaching beyond simple success metrics, that may not be possible or cost-effective in hardware-only research. Per-episode telemetry provides minimum clearance, time-to-collision (TTC), maneuver latency, and path deviation measurements relevant to DAA performance envelopes. Deterministic acceptance tests and specific scenario suites support side-by-side comparison across policy variants and random seeds; while animation exports provide visual evidence suitable for pilot and safety-engineer review.The trained models are capable of detecting and avoiding both static and moving obstacles with a high reliability while reaching assigned goals without collision or boundary violation. A mission-execution wrapper allows users to specify these key locations via a command-line interface, enabling rapid scenario generation without recompilation. Each mission is first executed in simulation, producing a CSV telemetry file that is then consumed by a Python-based Crazyflie flight controller. Real-world execution uses Crazyflie’s built-in library to perform waypoint navigation with optional live plotting and configurable safety parameters, including goal radius, obstacle proximity thresholds, and speed limits. Missions conclude with automated reporting of success, collision, out-of-bounds, or timeout outcomes, followed by autonomous takeoff, path execution, and landing. Future work includes higher-fidelity sensor models (ADS-B, radar, and vision), formalized curriculum rules tied to quantitative risk thresholds for airspace authorization, and expanded sim-to-real transfer studies to assess readiness for deployment in both reserved corridors and mixed cooperative/non-cooperative airspace. The intermediary CSV creation/ingestion can also be simplified away in favor of real-time streaming of the telemetry data directly to the Crazyflie control program.

title: Surrogate modeling of aerodynamic coefficients for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle design
abstract: In the field of aircraft aerodynamic design and optimization, the use of surrogate models has emerged as a powerful tool for reducing computational costs. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations are one of the highest computational expenses of developing a digital twin for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). In order to mitigate this expense, this study aims to evaluate the properties of Gaussian Process Regression algorithms in comparison to N-dimensional linear interpolators and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for use in the creation of a digital twin for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). An experimental analysis was conducted utilizing actual aerodynamic data from CFD simulations of a vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) UAV. The results of this study indicate that Gaussian Process Regressors (GPRs) are the most suitable choice for estimating aerodynamic coefficients as a function of roll, pitch, and yaw angles.

title: Sensing-Task-Oriented Generative Channel Model for 6G Integrated Sensing and Communications
abstract: Accurate and efficient channel modeling is paramount for the performance evaluation of 6G integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, conventional methods face a critical trade-off among accuracy, generalization, and computational complexity, hindering large-scale system-level simulations. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel sensing-task-oriented generative channel model tailored for target localization, tracking, and identification. Our approach is founded on a transformer-based conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) that learns to generate realistic multiple scattering center (MSC) attributes from highfidelity full-wave electromagnetic simulation data of vehicle and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) targets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a superior balance of these competing requirements. Notably, it reproduces channel characteristics with high fidelity while accelerating channel generation by a factor of one million compared to direct simulation. Furthermore, through task-oriented validation, our model shows significant performance advantages over traditional statistical models, particularly in collaborative sensing scenarios, which is a hallmark of future 6G ISAC. This work provides a foundational and computationally efficient tool for realistic performance evaluation of next-generation ISAC systems.

title: Modeling and Analysis of Vegetation Effects in UAV Network Coverage Prediction with LiDAR and NVIDIA SionnaRT
abstract: Realistic simulation of radio frequency (RF) signal behavior is essential for both wireless communication and microwave remote sensing. Exact RF coverage maps for base stations and UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) are becoming a key focus area to optimize system performance, enhance signal coverage, and ensure reliable data transmission and retrieval in remote sensing and communication applications. An accurate digital representation of the physical environment can offer optimized solutions for system design and deployment challenges before real-world testing. In real environments, signals can weaken or get blocked due to multipath propagation and obstructions from trees, terrain, and buildings. Traditional ray-tracing tools based on statistical Monte Carlo methods can model direct paths, specular reflections, and diffuse reflections. However, a major challenge is that different landscapes contain different types of trees, and their height, leaf density, and structure produce unique scattering patterns. Existing ray-tracing tools that rely on stochastic models to capture these parameters tend to be computationally expensive, time inefficient, and limited in realistic visualization.

title: Design and Implementation of a VTOL UAV and its Digital Twin
abstract: In this paper, we adopted a VTOL UAV model design and developed a digital twin for the corresponding model. The digital twin consists of the following parts: Unity simulation system, physical VTOL UAV, and communication interface. As we know, the main function of the digital twin is verification. However, there is a gap between the virtual simulation and physical test results. Therefore, based on the Unity engine and the VTOL UAV, this paper will demonstrate a simulation case of performing short takeoff and vertical landing operations using the VTOL UAV. These simulation results show that the system can simulate the aerodynamics, physics, and controls of the UAV with high fidelity and reliability. The digital twin system can also provide a platform for VTOL UAV application development, theoretical investigation, and intelligent training.

title: Big-Data-Driven ISAR RF Digital Twin for UAV Channel Modeling in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
abstract: This paper extends an ISAR based RF digital twin framework by incorporating big data technologies to model unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication channels in sixth generation non terrestrial networks (6G NTNs). High resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) echoes, vehicle trajectories, network telemetry and environmental context are collected via an edge–cloud data pipeline. Lightweight preprocessing at the edge performs motion and Doppler compensation and compresses radar echoes into compact spectral–temporal descriptors, while distributed storage and processing in the cloud facilitate large scale training and real time decision making. A Transformer backbone fuses ISAR features with trajectory and context signals, and a reinforcement learning engine adapts beamforming, power allocation and scheduling. Novel freshness aware state variables ensure the digital twin remains synchronized with rapid UAV attitude changes and blockage conditions, and anomaly detection triggers recalibration when sensor drift is detected. Simulations across urban, suburban and open environments show that the big data enhanced twin achieves lower outage probability, reduced end to end latency and higher throughput than statistical, CNN based or ray tracing baselines, illustrating the value of combining ISAR detail, big data pipelines and edge intelligence in 6G NTN scenarios.

title: A Digital Twin Framework for Multi-UAV and U-Space Operations with Real-Time Testing Integration
abstract: The digital twin paradigm is increasingly recognized as a key enabler for advancing autonomy, safety, and operational reliability in unmanned aviation. This paper presents a digital twin-based simulation framework designed for single and multi-UAV operations, integrating offline and real-time execution modes within a unified environment. The system combines high-fidelity dynamic models of multiple UAV platforms with a MAVLink-based communication layer that ensures seamless interoperability with ground control stations such as QGroundControl and Mission Planner. In addition, the framework incorporates an interface to a U-Space Service Provider (USSP), enabling the evaluation of U-Space services and procedures in realistic operational scenarios. This integration supports real-time testing, hardware-in-the-loop experiments, and the assessment of cooperative mission behaviors under varying traffic and airspace conditions. By providing a controllable and risk-free environment, the digital twin reduces development time, cost, and safety concerns associated with real flight testing, while enabling both technical and operational performance evaluations. The paper describes the system architecture, key functionalities, and experimental capabilities, and outlines future research directions for enhancing digital-twin-enabled UAV and U-Space operations.

title: Community Based Cyber-Physical Systems for Urban Waste Management: A Socio-Technical Innovation Model in the Fenicia Urban Living Lab
abstract: This manuscript presents an urban experiment on waste management developed under the Technological Innovation Management Model of the Urban Living Lab (ULL) in Fenicia, Bogotá. The model enables the co-creation of socio-technical solutions by integrating community participation, digital technologies, and iterative experimentation to address urban challenges. In this case, the experiment focuses on the detection and simulation of street waste through a cyber-physical system (CPS) that leverages artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, and citizen sensing. Community members use drones and smart-phones to capture georeferenced images of waste, particularly plastic bottles, discarded in public spaces. These images are uploaded to a digital twin platform where a custom-trained AI model identifies and classifies the waste. The digital twin then simulates spatial accumulation patterns and critical dumping points, providing actionable insights for decision-making and urban intervention. This paper shows an IA-driven recognition, proposing a scalable to a real-time simulation, of a model on socio-technical innovation. The results contribute to building a replicable model for smart waste management in developing countries.

title: Models of Availability Assessing UAV-based Systems for Monitoring Dangerous Space Considering Human Machine Interface with Embedded AR
abstract: Modern systems for forest fire monitoring, humanitarian demining, critical infrastructure control, and other dangerous or potentially dangerous spaces require the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). To improve their effectiveness, these systems also require the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud technologies, digital twins, and other advanced tools. One such technology is augmented reality (AR), which, when applied in humanmachine interaction (HMI) tools, has the potential to enhance the user experience of UAV operators and significantly reduce the number of errors made during task execution. The objectives of this study are to: (a) develop a simplified architecture of a dangerous spaces monitoring system focused on the interaction between the operator and the UAV; (b) develop a prototype of a HMI using AR technology for UAV operators; (c) develop Markov models that both exclude and include the possibility of operator error during UAV control, for subsequent comparison and assessment of their impact on the system. The main contribution is the AR-based HMI prototype for UAV control as part of a hazardous area monitoring system and results of simulation of suggested Markov models considering UAV operator reaction time and risk of errors.

title: MorphoMove: Bi-Modal Path Planner with MPC-based Path Follower for Multi-Limb Morphogenetic UAV
abstract: This paper discusses developments for a multi-limb morphogenetic UAV, MorphoGear, that is capable of both aerial flight and ground locomotion. A hybrid path planning algorithm based on the A* strategy has been developed, enabling seamless transition between air-to-ground navigation modes, thereby enhancing robot's mobility in complex environments. Moreover, precise path following is achieved during ground locomotion with a Model Predictive Control (MPC) architecture for its novel walking behaviour. Experimental validation was conducted in the Unity simulation environment utilizing Python scripts to compute control values. The algorithm's performance is validated by the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.91 cm and a maximum error of 1.85 cm, as demonstrated by the results. These developments highlight the adaptability of MorphoGear in navigation through cluttered environments, establishing it as a usable tool in autonomous exploration, both aerial and ground-based.

title: Integration of Digital Photogrammetry in the Three-Dimensional Modeling of Built Heritage
abstract: Aerial digital photogrammetry offers a viable alternative to traditional surveying, providing higher accuracy, lower operational costs, and a non-destructive approach ideal for mapping heritage sites. UAV's successfully capture 3D models of structures, accurately reproducing complex geometries at various resolutions. Our research presents a structured methodology for accurate 3D representation, involving the precision alignment of UAV imagery, GNSS RTK positioning for Ground Control Points (GCP's), and independent verification using a total station. From the aligned images, we generate dense point clouds, create orthophotographs, and vectorise facade surfaces into formats suitable for architectural analysis. The resulting metric measurements provide sufficient detail for precise architectural analysis, restoration planning, and long-term digital preservation. Beyond restoration, the georeferenced 3D model serves as a foundational building block for Virtual Reality (VR) applications and Digital Twins of heritage sites. These models allow users to evaluate cultural assets in unprecedented detail, interact with them innovatively, and simulate structural changes caused by natural or man-made disasters. Ultimately, aerial digital photogrammetry is a key component in creating a framework for the digital documentation and preservation of architectural heritage. This methodology opens numerous possibilities for multidisciplinary growth, particularly in developing immersive 3D models and visualizing them through virtual reality.

title: Process Mining for Reliability Modeling of Manufacturing Systems with Limited Data Availability
abstract: Accurate reliability modeling of manufacturing systems results in reduced maintenance costs and increased profits. The growing research field of data-driven reliability modeling seeks to harness the abundance of data from Smart Manufacturing Systems to improve and automate reliability modeling processes. Many manufacturing systems, however, still collect very limited amounts and types of data (typically operational state logs of production resources), which, we believe, can still be made useful to extract meaningful and useful reliability models. This motivates the work-in-progress that we present in this paper, a proof-of-concept method that extracts reliability models from state logs of production resources with deterministic durations of activities. First, the process model of a manufacturing system is extracted using a simple, yet efficient algorithm. Second, the reliability distributions for each production asset are fitted and useful reliability insights are integrated into the previously extracted process model. We conduct experiments of our proposed method using state logs from a drone manufacturing environment that is part of our university Industry 4.0 laboratory. The results show that a high-level overview of a system and its reliability can be provided with minimal data requirements and limited expert knowledge of the system. To this end, we also propose possible extensions and further developments of our method to make it more applicable to more challenging scenarios.

title: Standardized Digital Twin Framework for Modeling, Monitoring, and Detection of Cyber–Physical Threats in Photovoltaic Plant Sensors
abstract: This article presents a cost-effective and real-time digital twin (DT) framework for cyber–physical anomaly detection, monitoring, and modeling in photovoltaic (PV) plants. The proposed approach employs open-source tools, such as OpenModelica, and integrates the functional mock-up interface (FMI) standard to create portable, scalable, and interoperable functional mock-up units (FMUs). These FMUs serve as dynamic virtual representations of the physical system, enabling continuous estimation, tracking, and recognition of abnormal behavior in real time. The framework is validated using a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform that emulates realistic PV plant operations, providing a controlled environment for testing and verification. In addition, the DT runs on a low-cost single board computer (SBC), comparing real-time sensor measurements with model-based estimations to accurately detect anomalies without requiring extensive computational resources. For effective data analysis and visualization, the system uses open-source time-series database solutions, facilitating early detection and traceability of cyber–physical threats. By integrating measurement and monitoring functions with behavioral modeling and anomaly detection into a unified, standardized framework, this work supports the detection and analysis of cyber–physical security threats in PV plant sensors, contributing to more reliable, efficient, and accessible system monitoring.

title: Secured Surveillance Through Digital Twins and DDoS Attack Detection in 5G/6G-Oriented FANET
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks pose a serious threat to Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs), where highly mobile UAV nodes rely on stable, low-latency communication for mission-critical operations. This paper presents a Digital Twin (DT)-enabled DDoS detection framework that combines machine-learning-based flow classification with a realistic NS-3 simulation of a 6 G -oriented UAV network. The system models UAVs, Road-Side Units (RSUs), and a DT node communicating over ad hoc Wi-Fi using Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR), while generating both benign telemetry and networklayer DDoS traffic. Flow-level statistical features are extracted at RSUs and streamed to the DT for preprocessing, MutualInformation (MI)-based feature selection, and federated logisticregression training.
